items.prompt: Black's bishop has just taken your knight on f3. Two pieces can recapture there. Write the position each recapture leads to in your head, compare them, and find the better recapture.

claims.statement: Qxf3 is the engine's best move.
Recapturing with the pawn is clearly worse.
Both Qxf3 and gxf3 are legal recaptures.

hints: Both recaptures win the bishop back, so material cannot decide. What else differs between the two positions?
Look at your pawns and your king after each recapture.
Recapture with the queen.
items.explain: Both moves win the bishop back, so a material count ties. The engine still rates Qxf3 clearly better, because the positions differ in other ways. Comparing the whole resulting position, not only the material, is the skill.

feedback_by_move.g2f3: gxf3 recaptures too, but the engine rates the position it leaves clearly worse.

items.prompt: Both Qxf6 and gxf6 win the bishop back, and the queen recapture looks more natural. Is Qxf6 as good as gxf6? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: gxf6 is the engine's best move.
Qxf6 is far worse than gxf6.
gxf6 loses no material along the engine's line.

hints: Follow Qxf6 one more move. Can White take the queen with something cheaper?
After Qxf6, which White piece attacks the queen on f6?
A rook takes the queen on f6; Black retakes with a pawn.
items.explain: After Qxf6 a White rook can take the queen on f6, and Black only gets a rook back. The pawn recapture gxf6 spoils Black's pawns but keeps the queen. The first idea (the piece you like) is not always the best recapture.

feedback_by_move.e7f6: Qxf6 Rxf6 gxf6 trades Black's queen for a rook: the engine rates this far worse.

items.prompt: White is in check. Is there anything to compare here, or is the choice already made? Is more than one legal move available?

claims.statement: White is in check.
White has exactly one legal move, Kxe2.

hints: Count White's legal moves.
Can White block, capture with another piece, or move the king elsewhere?
Only the king can capture the checking queen, and it has no other square.
items.explain: White has one legal move, Kxe2, so there is nothing to compare. Comparing positions costs time and only pays when there are real alternatives.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawn has just taken on f6. Find the best recapture.

claims.statement: Nxf6 is the engine's best move.
Bxf6 is far worse.

hints: Two Black pieces can retake on f6. Compare where each recapture leaves the other piece.
One recapture leaves a Black piece on a square where it is soon attacked.
Retake with the knight.
items.explain: Both recaptures win the pawn back; the engine rates the knight recapture clearly better than the bishop recapture. A tie in material is where the comparison starts, not where it ends.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: bxc6 is the engine's best move.
Qxc6 is far worse.

hints: List the legal recaptures, then picture the position after each.
Check what the queen recapture allows next.
Retake with the pawn.
items.explain: The queen recapture walks into a rook capture; the pawn recapture keeps everything. Picture the position after each candidate before you decide.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxe4 is the engine's best move.
dxe4 is far worse.

hints: There is a piece to retake. How many ways are there?
Picture the position after each way of retaking.
Retake with the bishop.
items.explain: Both pieces can retake on e4. The bishop recapture keeps White's structure and the pawn recapture runs into trouble on the h4 knight's side; the engine rates dxe4 far worse.

items.prompt: Black can take the b2 pawn with the queen. If you stop calculating after Qxb2, it wins a pawn and attacks a rook. Does Qxb2 really win material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qxb2 loses material along the engine's line.
Qxb2 is far worse than the best move.

hints: Count the plies. How far did you look?
After Qxb2, what does the knight on c3 attack?
The knight can go to a4 and the queen runs out of squares.
items.explain: A line that stops at Qxb2 sees a free pawn. Two plies later Na4 attacks the queen, and every queen move loses material. Forcing lines have to be followed until the position is quiet.

items.prompt: Black to move. Every move in the best line is a check or a capture, so follow it until the end. Find the winning first move.

claims.statement: Qxf2+ forces checkmate in three.
Qxf2+ is the engine's best move.
Rxf2 is clearly worse.

hints: Put the checks and captures on your list. Which one gives something up?
Black can give up the queen. Follow the checks that come afterwards.
Queen takes f2 with check, and the rook comes in with another check.
items.explain: Qxf2+ gives up the queen for a pawn, so a short look rejects it. The forcing line continues Rxf2 Rd1+ Rf1 Rdxf1 mate. When every move is a check or a capture, calculation can go deep because the number of replies stays small.

items.prompt: White to move. Is this a critical moment (a tempting move that costs a lot) or a routine one (many moves are about equal)?

claims.statement: The tempting capture Nxe4 is far worse than the best move.
Qf4 is the engine's best move.

hints: Is there a capture on the board that looks free?
Ask what happens if you play it. Does the engine agree?
The pawn on e4 can be taken, but the capture is the costly mistake.
items.explain: Nxe4 looks like a free pawn but loses to a knight check that wins material, so this is a moment to spend time. A moment with a tempting capture or a forcing line is where deep checking pays.

items.prompt: Black to move. Critical moment, or routine one?

claims.statement: The tempting capture Nxc5 is far worse than the best move.
Rb8 is the engine's best move.

hints: Look for captures that seem to win a piece.
A capture is tempting here. Check what White can answer with a check.
The knight capture on c5 allows a rook check on the back rank.
items.explain: Nxc5 takes a knight but allows a rook check that wins more. A tempting capture with a forcing reply is the sign of a moment worth the thinking time.

items.prompt: White to move. Critical moment, or routine one?

claims.statement: The engine's best move is one of three moves that are all within 40 centipawns of it.
No line wins more than a pawn for White.

hints: Look for a capture or a check that changes the material.
If you find none, ask how different the sensible moves really are.
Several sensible moves score about the same.
items.explain: No forcing line wins material and three sensible moves are within 40 centipawns of each other. A long calculation here has almost nothing to find; pick a sensible move and keep your time for later.

items.prompt: White to move. Critical moment, or routine one?

claims.statement: The engine's best move is one of three moves that are all within 40 centipawns of it.
No line wins more than a pawn for White.

hints: Look for a capture or a check that changes the material.
Do the sensible developing moves differ much in value?
Three different plans score within a fraction of a pawn.
items.explain: No forcing line wins material and three different plans are within 40 centipawns of each other. Depth is a budget; this is a position to spend little of it on.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qc2+ forces checkmate in three.
Qc2+ is the engine's best move.

hints: Which of your moves are checks? Follow them until a line ends.
Some of the checks give up the queen. Keep following.
Queen checks, the king steps aside, the queen checks again and a rook finishes.
items.explain: Qc2+ Ka1 Qc1+ Rxc1 Rxc1 is checkmate. The line is five plies long and every move is forcing, so it can be followed to the end.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qxf1+ forces checkmate in three.
Qxf1+ is the engine's best move.

hints: Which of your moves are checks? Follow them until a line ends.
One check gives up the queen. See what follows.
The queen takes with check, the king takes, and a knight check comes next.
items.explain: Qxf1+ Kxf1 Nd2+ Kg1 Re1 is checkmate. Giving up the queen only looks bad until you follow the forcing line to its end.

items.prompt: Black's queen has just taken the pawn on b2. White to move. Find White's best reply.

claims.statement: Rfb1 is the engine's best move.
Rfb1 wins material along the engine's line.
Rfe1 is far worse.

hints: The queen has gone far from home. How many safe squares does it have?
Attack the queen so that its squares disappear.
Bring a rook to the b-file.
items.explain: After Rfb1 the queen is attacked and has no safe square, so Black loses it for a rook. The player who took the pawn only looked at the pawn, not at White's reply.

items.prompt: White is thinking of taking the h7 pawn with the queen. Before you decide, look for Black's best reply: a check, a capture or a threat. Does Qxh7 work? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Qxh7 is far worse than the best move.
Qb5+ is the engine's best move.

hints: Start with Black's checks after Qxh7.
Where is White's king, and who guards the back rank?
A knight check followed by a rook check ends the game.
items.explain: After Qxh7 Black has Ne2+ and then a rook check on f1 that is mate. Looking at the opponent's checks first would have found it.

items.prompt: White's knight has just taken the pawn on e4. Black to move. Find Black's best reply.

claims.statement: Nb3+ is the engine's best move.
Rxd4 is clearly worse.

hints: Start with your checks. Which of your pieces can give one?
Check the squares your knight can reach. What else does it attack from there?
The knight checks from b3 and hits another piece as well.
items.explain: Nb3+ is a check that also attacks White's queen on d2, so Black wins material. Taking on e4 walked into the fork.

items.prompt: White to move. A capture is available. Check Black's best reply before you commit. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qxc5 is the engine's best move.
Qa4 is far worse.

hints: Look at the capture, then at Black's strongest answers: checks, captures, threats.
Does Black have a way to punish the capture?
Take the queen on c5.
items.explain: Qxc5 takes the queen, and Black's checks and captures do not repay it. Here the search for the opponent's best reply finds nothing, so the capture is safe.

items.prompt: White is thinking of Nxe5, taking a pawn. Check Black's best reply first. Does Nxe5 win a pawn? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Nxe5 loses material along the engine's line.
Nxe5 is far worse than the best move.

hints: After Nxe5, which Black piece can take the knight?
What lines open when the bishop takes on e5?
Bxe5 attacks the rook on a1 and the queen has an answer to everything else.
items.explain: Bxe5 takes the knight and attacks the rook on a1, and the queen on c3 cannot defend everything. Nxe5 wins a pawn only if Black cooperates.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Qf2 is checkmate.

hints: Check your own checks first.
Is there a move after which the opponent has no reply at all?
The queen goes to f2.
items.explain: Qf2 is checkmate, so the opponent's best reply does not exist. When you can mate, there is nothing to defend against and the search ends at once.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Nc6 is the engine's best move.
Qxd5 is far worse.

hints: A capture is available. Before you play it, look for White's checks.
White has a knight check that uncovers another attack.
A quiet developing move is best.
items.explain: Qxd5 wins a knight on the surface, but Ng5+ uncovers an attack on the black queen's file and White wins far more. The quiet developing move avoids it. A tempting capture is a cue to look for the reply.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Kf8 is the engine's best move.
Kxf7 is far worse.

hints: A bishop is attacked. Check what White can do if you take it.
After Kxf7 the king is exposed to a knight check that forks.
Step back instead of capturing.
items.explain: Kxf7 wins a bishop but Ng5+ forks the king and the queen on h3. Stepping aside with Kf8 keeps everything. Look for the reply before you take.
